subject: skill frontmatter versioning
fact: Workspace skills carry `metadata: version` in SKILL.md frontmatter alongside name/description; bump it on meaningful changes.
citations: skills/copilot-extension-builder/SKILL.md:4-5 (metadata version 0.2.1); skills/copilot-plugin-builder/SKILL.md (version 0.2.0); skills/copilot-session-telemetry/SKILL.md (version 0.4.0); grep across skills/*/SKILL.md shows ~25 skills with metadata.version
reason: The generic skill-creator skill mandates name+description only, but this repo consistently uses metadata.version across its skills, so future skill edits here must preserve and bump that field instead of stripping it. I initially removed it and had to restore it when the user requested a version bump.

subject: git commit skills division of labor
fact: The three git commit skills each own one meaning and must not restate the others: git-atomic-commit owns the type/scope tier tables and the pre-commit staging gate; git-commit-scope-constitution owns scope naming, granularity, and the single-scope mandate; git-session-atomic-commits owns only the allowlist boundary and delegates all other verification.
reason: These skills are tightly correlated and historically duplicated the three-tier table, the staging gate, and naming rules across files. Contributors adding rules must know which file is the single source of truth, or the duplication and context load will creep back.

subject: Subagent dispatch preamble
fact: Every subagent dispatch prompt in this repo must reference .github/subagent-dispatch.md (tool quirks, file-first report contract, spec-section→test mapping, gate command) instead of restating those blocks inline.
reason: During the fleet session the same ~6-line tool-quirk block was retyped into ~10 dispatch prompts, with drift risk per copy, and one critic ignored the file-first protocol until it was restated verbatim. Single-sourcing in a repo file referenced by one prompt line cuts tokens and keeps the protocol authoritative; future sessions need the file's path to use it.

subject: Linux CI test portability
fact: Pester tests and skill scripts must avoid Windows-only assumptions because the `ci` gate runs on ubuntu-latest: call bare `sqlite3` (PATHEXT resolves sqlite3.exe on Windows), never rely on `$env:TEMP` (unset on Linux; use [IO.Path]::GetTempPath()), and configure git user.name/user.email on fixture repos (CI runners have no global git identity).
reason: These three assumptions caused 32/145 Pester failures in the GitHub Actions gate while passing locally on Windows, so any future test or script work in skills/ must follow them or CI turns red again. Each fix was reproduced and verified green in a Linux container.

subject: Workflow push credentials
fact: Pushing commits that touch .github/workflows/** from this machine fails with "OAuth App ... without workflow scope" because Git Credential Manager's stored token lacks it; route the push through gh's keyring token: `git -c credential.helper= -c "credential.https://github.com.helper=!gh auth git-credential" push origin main`.
reason: Two push attempts were rejected before this was diagnosed; the credential.helper= reset is required because the URL-specific helper is appended after GCM otherwise and GCM answers first. Future CI-workflow edits will hit the same wall without this exact command.

subject: issue templates
fact: The issue-tracking skill gates every local issue file against per-type templates (assets/issue-templates/<type>.md); consumers override per type via manifest issueTemplatesDir + issueTemplateOverrides.
reason: Future edits to the issue store, the issue-tracking scripts, or any consumer repo's .github/issue-tracker.json must respect this enforced contract: unknown frontmatter fields and missing required body sections fail the gate. Knowing the template set's location and the override mechanism is required before filing issues or extending validation.

subject: issue taxonomy
fact: GitHub issue `type` is a first-class single-select field separate from labels (REST `type`, GraphQL `issueType`, `gh --json issueType`); defaults Task/Bug/Feature, up to 25 per owner.
reason: The issue-tracking skill models issue classification and grouping, and GitHub's native `type` field is the industry-standard vocabulary it must align to. Future edits to sync-github-tree.ps1, the template taxonomy, or any label-vs-type logic depend on knowing that `type` is distinct from `labels`, that `gh` exposes it as `issueType` (not `type`), and that values are owner-scoped with a 25-type cap rather than a fixed enum. Remembering this prevents regressions that re-conflate grouping labels with issue classification.

subject: issue taxonomy
fact: Issue `type` is classification only (default task/bug/feature, overridable via manifest `issueTypes`); grouping/theme is a `theme` label, with `type: theme` kept as a permanent legacy alias.
reason: The issue-tracking skill v2.0 deliberately splits the old conflated enum into two axes to align with GitHub, where the issue type field is a single-select that is not a label. Future work on issue files, templates, the tree gate, or the github sync must not reintroduce grouping values (theme/epic) into the default type vocabulary, and must keep `type: theme` accepted so migrated stores never break. Knowing this prevents silent regressions in gate behavior and template resolution.
